source.title: Fisher information and the geometry of memorization in neural networks
source.authors: Daniel T. Bernstein; Chase Goddard; L. di Carlo; Wave Ngampruetikorn; David J. Schwab

record.tranche_reason: Measures whether Fisher-based weight projections separate memorized examples or tasks from generalizing performance, using a different intervention and measure from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports Fisher-projection and sample-projection results on controlled input noise, label noise, and synthetic in-context tasks. Its results concern geometric separation of memorization and generalization; the text does not test the specific conditions or measures named by V1–V8.
record.test_reason: The study tests Fisher-based separation of memorization and generalization, which none of V1–V8 asserts. It does not compare natural-label learning with fully random-label learning, sweep training width, compare training recipes, measure magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps, or remove memorized examples and retrain. Its parameter projections therefore provide no verdict on these versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: Fisher geometry separates memorized and generalizing information in selected layers and settings, with strong dependence on the Fisher dataset. Suppressing some memorized directions can improve generalization without retraining. The authors explicitly limit their conclusions to the studied small models and controlled tasks and note that cross-layer correlations are ignored.
record.recipe_differences: Uses controlled input and label noise, Fisher-based weight projection, and synthetic in-context regression to study memorization/generalization geometry; it does not implement the listed versions' interventions or comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed separation depends on layer and on whether the Fisher is computed from clean or full training data; effects also differ between input noise, label noise, attention, and MLP components.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-Fisher projection preserves structured CIFAR-10 performance while suppressing Gaussian memorization in the first layer, but the final layer shows no such separation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fisher-based separation of controlled input memorization from generalization depends on layer.

fits_no_version.finding: For label noise, projections can partially recover true labels; separation in the penultimate convolutional layer weakens when noisy examples enter the Fisher estimate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fisher-based de-memorization depends on both layer and the data used to estimate the Fisher.

fits_no_version.finding: Second-block MLP projection recovers roughly half the lost held-out-task performance relative to early stopping, while attention projection harms both training-task and held-out-task performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fisher projection can partially recover synthetic in-context generalization in particular transformer components.

fits_no_version.finding: Input-noise samples concentrate toward lower Fisher modes, whereas corrupted and uncorrupted label-noise samples contribute in a constant ratio across modes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sample contributions to Fisher eigenspaces depend on the form of injected noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-sample Fisher projections have modest effects on bulk CIFAR accuracy, while Gaussian-targeted projections substantially reduce accuracy across the Gaussian set.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The collateral effects of single-sample parameter projections depend on the targeted sample distribution.

record.problems: Empirical vision results use ResNet-20 on CIFAR-10 variants with controlled input and label noise; the authors state that larger models may show qualitatively different layerwise separation. The analysis ignores cross-layer correlations. Some results are reported in figures, and numerical uncertainty is not stated for the cited projection outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows retained from the supplemental figures; they show other layers and control projections, but the text does not provide separately assignable numerical values for those curves.

untested.parts: The matched natural-label versus fully random-label training comparison and random-label held-out accuracy. Fitting injected noise alongside structured data does not supply that comparison; vision training also uses weight decay.
Test error as training width increases beyond interpolation. Retained projection rank is not network width.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Effects of adding, configuring, or removing dropout. Using dropout in the transformer is not a comparison.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps across similarly fitted networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence, retraining, and comparing the accuracy loss with matched random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures fit no version; this does not dispute the reported Fisher effects. No additional version-relevant results require missing entries. The study's related-work citations to original sources do not establish a test.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting arbitrary fixed random labels with fitting natural labels using the same architecture and recipe, or report random-label held-out accuracy.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
Measures Fisher eigenspaces and participation ratios, not magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness or its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Projects parameter directions; does not remove selected memorized training examples and retrain.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Projected first-layer weights onto top Fisher eigenvectors computed over full training set.
rows.measure: Classification accuracy on CIFAR-10 train, CIFAR-10 test, and memorized Gaussian samples
rows.value: CIFAR-10 train and test reach near-maximum accuracy; Gaussian accuracy remains less than 30%.
rows.note: The result describes selective de-memorization at negligible cost to CIFAR-10 generalization.
rows.check: The reported projection result is accurate but measures no listed version. The relevant reference is the unprojected model; training accuracy before projection is 100%. Train, test, and Gaussian accuracy should be separate measures.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Projected last-layer weights onto top Fisher eigenvectors computed over full training set.
rows.measure: Classification accuracy on CIFAR-10 train, CIFAR-10 test, and memorized Gaussian samples
rows.value: Accuracy across all three partitions climbs simultaneously to full-model accuracy as subspace dimension increases.
rows.note: The text reports no separation between memorized and structured representations in this layer.
rows.check: Absence of selective de-memorization is not absence of an effect asserted by V1–V8.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Projected first-layer weights onto top Fisher eigenvectors computed on clean data.
rows.measure: Accuracy on true labels of flipped samples
rows.value: Improves well above chance in the top Fisher subspace.
rows.note: Projection does not completely remove memorized data; true-label recovery improves.
rows.check: True-label recovery after weight projection measures no listed version. Chance is a reference level; the fully fitted model predicts the assigned wrong labels, giving zero true-label accuracy on these samples.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Projected penultimate convolutional-layer weights onto top Fisher eigenvectors computed on clean data.
rows.measure: Accuracy on flipped samples under assigned and true labels, and train/test accuracy
rows.value: The red curve has not reached its maximum by the time train and test accuracy do; true-label accuracy rises well above chance.
rows.note: Text characterizes clean-Fisher de-memorization as successful in this layer.
rows.check: The result concerns projection-based separation and partial true-label recovery, not a listed version. The row combines multiple accuracy measures.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Projected penultimate convolutional-layer weights onto top Fisher eigenvectors computed on the full training set.

conditions.value: full training set, including noisy labels

rows.measure: Accuracy curves for clean and flipped-label data
rows.value: Accuracy curves move closer together; decoupling becomes weaker.
rows.note: The result is explicitly contrasted with using only clean samples to compute the Fisher.
rows.check: Dependence of de-memorization on the Fisher dataset measures no listed version. The full Fisher is estimated using a subset sampled from the full training dataset.

rows.subject: three-block GPT-2 style transformer
rows.size_stated: hidden dimension 32; 8 attention heads in each block
rows.stage_stated: trained on synthetic in-context regression task
rows.operation_detail: Projected second-block attention-layer parameters onto top Fisher subspaces.
rows.measure: MSE on memorized training tasks and held-out test tasks
rows.value: All projections decrease performance on both memorized training tasks and held-out test tasks.
rows.uncertainty: standard deviation across 16 models shown as shaded region
rows.note: The projection does not improve held-out task performance for attention.
rows.check: Attention projection harms training-task and held-out-task performance, but neither outcome measures a listed version.

rows.subject: three-block GPT-2 style transformer
rows.size_stated: hidden dimension 32; 8 attention heads in each block
rows.stage_stated: trained on synthetic in-context regression task
rows.operation_detail: Projected second-block MLP parameters onto top Fisher subspaces.
rows.measure: MSE on memorized training tasks and held-out test tasks
rows.value: Top Fisher subspaces improve task generalization at the cost of performance on memorized tasks; projection partially restores in-context generalization, closing roughly half the gap to the best early-stopped performance.
rows.note: The text reports this effect for the MLP component; other components are not combined into this row.
rows.check: Improved task generalization after parameter projection does not test V8's removal of memorized training examples and retraining.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Measured sample participation ratios across the layerwise Fisher eigenspectrum.
rows.measure: Participation ratios by eigenspectrum position and sample group
rows.value: Total participation ratios drop by roughly one order of magnitude from top to bottom modes; clean CIFAR-10 images dominate top modes, while memorized Gaussian noise is relegated to the bottom.
rows.note: This is a measured Fisher participation-ratio pattern, not magnitude-aware sharpness.
rows.check: Fisher participation ratios do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its association with generalization gaps.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Measured sample participation ratios across the layerwise Fisher eigenspectrum.
rows.measure: Participation ratios by eigenspectrum position and sample group
rows.value: Corrupted and uncorrupted samples contribute in a constant ratio across the entire spectrum.
rows.note: Unlike the input-noise experiment, the text reports no top-versus-bottom separation for these sample groups.
rows.check: The constant participation-ratio pattern measures no listed version; its recorded observed state describes that pattern, not a claim effect.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Projected out top eigenvectors of individual sample Fisher information matrices.
rows.measure: Bulk accuracy on CIFAR-10 train, CIFAR-10 test, and Gaussian set
rows.baseline: At k = 0: CIFAR-10 train 100.0%; CIFAR-10 test 84.3%; Gaussian set 100.0%.
rows.value: At k = 9: CIFAR-10 train 99.8%; CIFAR-10 test 83.1%; Gaussian set 75.6%.
rows.note: Gaussian-targeted sample projection degrades the Gaussian set while bulk CIFAR accuracy changes modestly.
rows.check: The row combines different Fisher sources. The 99.8% train and 83.1% test values at k=9 use CIFAR-targeted projections; 75.6% Gaussian accuracy uses Gaussian-targeted projections. For Gaussian targeting, Table 2 gives 100.0% CIFAR train and 83.4% CIFAR test accuracy. Split by Fisher source and measure. The operation edits weights rather than removing training examples.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Projected out top eigenvectors of individual sample Fisher information matrices.
rows.note: The table reports modest test-accuracy degradation as more sample-Fisher directions are projected out.
rows.check: The 73.4% to 72.3% test-accuracy change is correctly transcribed for uncorrupted-sample targeting. It is a weight edit, not example removal and retraining, and therefore does not test V8.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
